title: How to run a concept test: Methods, examples, and best practices
summary: Learn how to run concept testing, from choosing the right method and stimulus to analyzing consumer feedback and making decisions.
body_markdown:
What is concept testing? +


Concept testing is research used to evaluate an idea with potential customers before it's fully developed. A concept test can show whether people understand the idea and see value in it. The strongest concept testing research goes beyond a rating or preference score to uncover why people reacted that way.


What are some examples of concept testing? +


Concept testing examples can range from comparing new product ideas in the discovery phase to testing a value proposition before a product launch. For example, a consumer packaged goods brand might use a concept screening survey to compare several new snack concepts and identify the most promising concept for full-scale development. A brand might also test different packaging or positioning ideas to understand customer preferences and how each option affects brand perception.


How is concept testing different from usability testing? +


Concept testing asks whether an idea works for the target audience before it has been built. Usability testing asks whether people can use a working product or prototype successfully. In simple terms, concept testing helps you decide whether an idea is worth developing, while usability testing helps you find problems with something you've already built.


What's the difference between concept testing and focus groups? +


Concept testing evaluates how individual consumers respond to a specific product idea, while focus groups use a moderated group discussion to explore people's opinions and reactions. Concept testing is useful when you need to compare responses across a target audience and understand what drives those responses. Focus groups are useful when the group discussion can help uncover how people think about or react to an idea.


What's the difference between monadic and sequential monadic testing? +


Monadic testing shows each participant one concept, so their reaction is not shaped by another concept they have just seen. Sequential monadic testing shows participants several concepts one at a time, usually in a randomized order. It lets you compare concepts while still capturing each reaction on its own.


How do you know if a concept test result is reliable? +


A useful concept test gives you more than a score. The stimulus needs to be clear, the questions need to avoid leading participants, and the sample needs to reflect the target audience. Most importantly, you should be able to understand what sits behind the result. If a concept scores poorly, for example, the research should help explain whether people misunderstood it or couldn't see when they would use it.
